clue.text: Erasmus made good use of the rubber

indicators.note: the letters of the scholar's name are put to good use by being rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: The Dutch humanist Erasmus put an eraser to good use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erasmus' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is just fodder: 'made good use of' tells you to rearrange its seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is one who rubs, and a person who gives massages is a professional rubber.

clue.text: Clever people join a top man in hiding

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree, clever people
the king is the top man

explanation.surface: Bright folk teaming up with the boss while lying low.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealing or covering up is masking.

clue.text: A lackadaisical worker made to move smartly

explanation.surface: An idle employee being made to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: To scamp work is to do it carelessly, so one who scamps is a lackadaisical worker.
explanation.definitionFit: One who skimps his work; and to run or scurry quickly.

clue.text: Creating sheer chaos in town

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters of the word sheer are jumbled

explanation.surface: Utter disorder breaking out in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: ESHER is a town in Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter settlement in Surrey is the town named.

clue.text: Made up, having changed

explanation.surface: Wearing makeup after a change of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as RE-DRESSED: dressed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensated for a wrong; and clothed again after changing.

clue.text: Talk when caught by a mad character

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Someone talks when cornered by an eccentric figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad character' points to the Hatter at Lewis Carroll's tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk or prattle is a synonym, both as noun and verb.

clue.text: The painter must be firm over rubbish

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over the other

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: An artist told to be strict about nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Camille Corot was a French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century French landscape artist.

clue.text: Criminals — oafs going around wrong-doing

indicators.note: the oafs encircle the wrong-doing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: two oafs, each an ass, written one after the other
a sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers, louts out committing offences.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'oafs' as two of them, each a donkey, and the wrong-doing goes in before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Killers hired to murder are criminals.

clue.text: Ground for surrounding the monarch with attendants

indicators.note: the attendants are around the monarch, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a train is a retinue of attendants
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Land set aside for courtiers to escort the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Land or terrain is the ground over which one travels.

clue.text: To break up requires courage

explanation.surface: Breaking off a relationship takes nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: To resolve is to separate something into its parts, a chemist's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate into components; and firmness of purpose, determination.

clue.text: Remains in vehicle, being wounded

indicators.note: the remains are placed inside the vehicle, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sled or sledge is a vehicle on runners
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A body found in a car, having been injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut with a blade is to be wounded by slashing.

clue.text: Re-classifies places for holidaymakers

explanation.surface: Someone reorganising holiday destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as RE-SORTS: sorts again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-sort is to classify again; seaside towns visited on holiday are resorts.

clue.text: Inadequate, so tense

explanation.surface: Something not up to scratch, so feeling strained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervous, but it is the grammar term: the past tense for incomplete action.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawed means not perfect; in grammar a past tense of ongoing action is called imperfect.

clue.text: Come to a stop, the way everybody should do

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
everybody means all

explanation.surface: A halt that the whole road should observe.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that cuts out and halts is said to stall.

clue.text: Plant this rose variety after spring's end

indicators.note: the rearranged rose follows the letter from spring in the answer
the end of the word spring is its final letter
a variety of the rose is taken as a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Advice to plant a rose cultivar once spring is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring's end' is the letter at the end of the season's name, not the end of springtime; the shuffled flower comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze, a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, is another name for this plant.

clue.text: Simple optical aid

explanation.surface: An uncomplicated aid to vision.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'simple' is an old word for a medicinal herb, and this one was used to treat sore eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal herb is a simple, and this plant was a traditional remedy for eye complaints.

clue.text: Feeling for one in time perhaps

indicators.note: one is placed inside the word for time, a container signal

parts.note: a prison term, or time, is a sentence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sensing what doing time might be like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time perhaps' points to prison time served, a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensation or the capacity for awareness is the core meaning.

clue.text: Managed to overturn the salt when telling the tale

indicators.note: turning the word for managed upside down in a down entry reads it backwards

parts.note: ran means managed
an old salt is a sailor, and a rating is an ordinary sailor

explanation.surface: Spilling the salt while recounting a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Recounting a story is narration.

clue.text: He'll take issue, finding many over-kind

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
on as in resting upon, over
tender means kind and gentle

explanation.surface: A rival discovering that many people are excessively nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-kind' looks like one word meaning too nice, but the hyphen hides two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival who disputes or competes takes issue.

clue.text: No clues will be needed by this man of the law

indicators.note: the letters of the two words must be reshaped to give what is needed here

explanation.surface: A lawyer who needs no hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister or legal adviser is called counsel.

clue.text: Love without object

parts.note: no means without, as in no money
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Affection with no purpose behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is zero, as in a tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a score of zero is called love.

clue.text: Nick's music

explanation.surface: A man named Nick owns the tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick's' looks like a person's name with a possessive, but it is a notch: the 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch or scratch is a score; the written parts of an orchestral piece form a score.

clue.text: Manipulate work time and a note results!

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time
TE is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Handle a job, a period, and a musical note together.
explanation.definitionFit: To work or control a machine is to manipulate it.

clue.text: Possibly ten tear off to make appeal

indicators.note: possibly signals that the combined letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: off as in gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the word tear are disturbed

explanation.surface: Ten men ripped away to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Possibly' and 'off' signal rearrangement; in effect the seven letters of TEN TEAR are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead earnestly with someone.

clue.text: Not qualified to speak out

explanation.surface: Someone unlicensed to voice an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not qualified' means unqualified in the sense of complete, absolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute or downright, as in total nonsense; and to say aloud.

clue.text: Publication for country people-the non-male

parts.note: a state is a country
men means people

indicators.note: without the male pronoun he, so those letters are removed from the word

explanation.surface: A newsletter for rural folk, but excluding men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-male' takes HE out of 'the', leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A published declaration or account, such as a press release, is a statement.

clue.text: Cut, but not totally disheartened by it

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: Wounded but not fully dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'disheartened'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip or snip, as with sheep's wool.

clue.text: She's caused a large number to leave the USA

indicators.note: the large number departs from the country, so those letters are removed

parts.note: America is the USA
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A woman who caused a crowd to emigrate from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's' gives a girl's name; AM removed from AMERICA leaves ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so a woman, a she.

clue.text: Rocky English beach

indicators.note: rocky as in unsteady, so the letters of the nationality are shaken up

explanation.surface: A stony beach on England's coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like it describes the beach, but it is the signal to rearrange ENGLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach covered in pebbles is called this.

clue.text: Take off a little-trim it at each corner

indicators.note: only a small part of the run of words is taken, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Advice to shave a bit off the corners.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'trim it at each'; 'corner' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic or impersonate someone is to take them off.

clue.text: The girl could be slimmer!

parts.note: a remark about a girl's weight, read as a word for one who weighs less

explanation.definitionFit: Weighing less is being slimmer, and less heavy is a comparative of light.

clue.text: Most sober and virtuous person after a final home

indicators.note: the virtuous person follows the final home in the answer

parts.note: the grave is the last resting place
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: A saint who has gone to the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious and solemn in the highest degree, a superlative of grave.
